properties.name: The two unallocated capabilities are given owning parts
properties.rationale:
BOTH ANSWERS COME FROM THE SAME RULING, applied deliberately rather than by taste: `chg:allocation-follows-the-code-not-the-neighbour` (2026-08-25) — allocate to the module whose code implements the function, move it, do not dual-allocate.

WHY `cmp:service` AND NOT `cmp:main`. The refusal is not the flag. `--read-only` is parsed in `main.rs`, but the enforcement is `ReflowService::write_lock`, which every mutating handler must obtain and no write can avoid; making it fallible turned all 98 write sites into compile errors until each was handled, and it caught `share()` as a SECOND assembly point that had to inherit the mode or read-only would have held for the process and evaporated for every actual client. Allocating to the entry point would file the function against the switch rather than the guard, and would point somewhere the refusal is not if the mode ever becomes settable another way. `art:service` already REALIZED both `cmp:service` and this capability, so the two layers now agree instead of only one of them holding the answer — the cross-layer check that change event was created by.

WHY A NEW PART RATHER THAN `cmp:temporal`. `manual_work.rs` is a real source module with a linked, checksummed artifact and no part of its own — the same shape as the 31 modules the 2026-08-25 sweep found. Crediting it to `cmp:temporal` because both write TemporalFacts is exactly the neighbour-misfiling that sweep corrected in 19 places, and it would have been a fresh instance of the class the day after the correction. `cmp:tools-temporal`, where the two tools are declared, is excluded by `dec:the-tool-surface-slices-hold-no-function-of-their-own`. Filing it by purpose under `sub:session-posture` was offered and declined for the same reason.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT SETTLE, and it was named when the choice was put: whether reflow2 should keep minting a part per module at all. Every leaf here is a module, so "which part owns this function" and "which file implements it" have collapsed into one question — which makes allocation cheap to get right and makes the allocation layer a second copy of the file tree. `dec:bl83a-functional-decomposition` holds the line at the SYSTEM level (functional, not the file tree) and says nothing about the leaves. That is a decomposition-grain decision nobody has made.

The containment `sys:time-history CONTAINS cmp:manual-work` skips the subsystem rung, which `hierarchy_issues` will read as a missing intermediate level. Done knowingly: all six existing children of `sys:time-history` sit the same way, so this matches its siblings rather than inventing a subsystem for one module. If that rung is ever added it should be added for all seven at once.
properties.subject: record
properties.summary: The design's only two open gaps were both `unallocated_capability`, on the two capabilities that landed in #350 and #351. Both are now owned, on Anthony's word 2026-08-26. "A server can refuse every write" → `cmp:service`, where `ReflowService::write_lock` enforces it. "A session records the work it did by hand" → `cmp:manual-work`, a NEW part created for `crates/reflow2-core/src/manual_work.rs`, contained by `sys:time-history` alongside `cmp:temporal`, with `art:manual-work` REALIZES it so the artifact layer and the allocation layer agree.
